language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.

Hi, I am the Little Mermaid and my name is Ariel. I live in the North Sea near Denmark. When I am not sitting on my favorite rock I like to go out and play – sometimes in the Ocean or sometimes on land. Join me and my friend Tim as we explore and learn about Light and Dark.

Our world is full of light. During the day, most of our light comes from the sun. At the end of the day it gets dark because the sun goes down. Light lets us see colors and things. Darkness is when there is no light. When there is no light, you cannot see anything.

All light must come from a source. A light source is something that produces light. Some of the sources are natural, like the sun, lightening or fire. Light can also be made by living things, for example by fireflies and glow fish.
There are also man-made light sources that create light from electricity. These include light bulbs, flashlights, lanterns, traffic lights and computer light.
You see, there is a lot to explore. Let’s go!
Okay, Ariel. This is going to be fun!

dialog.text: My pearl necklace broke and fell on the beach. It is dark, so I can not find the beads! Can you tell me which objects can help me see in the dark?
Ariel needs light to look for the broken necklace! Can you give her an object that will give her light?
Thank you, I found my necklace!

Light travels in straight lines. When light hits an object, some or all of the light is blocked, creating an area on the other side of the object with less light or no light. This dimmer area is called a shadow.

A shadow shows the shape of an object, but it does not show colors or details. As you move a light source around an object, the shadow of this object moves and the length and shape of the shadow changes.
I see many shadows all day long. Can you help me identify which shadow belongs to which object?
